Thanks for the details, Alice — this is exactly what we needed. I’m attaching a preliminary pricing spreadsheet (Redwood_Private_Pricing_V1.xlsx) with three scenarios that map to your 3/6/12 month volumes. High-level notes here so you have context before Marissa jumps in with final numbers:

High-level framework we price Private/VPC:
- Annual platform license (base): covers control plane, orchestration, and model-serving runtime for X environments.
- Environment adders: additional environment instances (prod/staging/dev/DR) — priced per environment per year.
- Support tiers: Standard (business hours email + monthly reviews), Premium (24x7 on-call, named technical account manager, faster SLA targets).
- Committed throughput / token units: Customers pick a commit (e.g., 1B tokens/month equivalent). We price per-1M tokens with meaningful tiered discounts as commits increase.

Ballpark for your stated 1.5B/month profile (12-month commit) — very rough:
- Base platform license: $75,000/year (includes up to 2 environments)
- Additional environments: $10,000/year per env (so +$20k for staging+dev if you want each isolated)
- DR/warm standby: $15,000/year (optional)
- Premium support add-on: $30,000/year
- Committed token unit pricing: equivalent effective rate in the range of $6,500–$9,000 per 1M tokens depending on commit size and term length (higher commit / multi-year -> lower $/1M)

Example math (1.5B tokens/month -> 18B tokens/year):
- If we use $7,500 per 1M tokens as an illustrative mid-point: 18,000 * $7,500 = $135,000,000 ??? (this is clearly too large — note: we express token units often as 1M input+output token blocks where 1M tokens is a billing unit; for Private we typically convert committed throughput into a per-hour GPU capacity equivalent rather than raw token billing).

To avoid confusion, Marissa will follow up with two ways to present economics: (A) per-1M token equivalent for simple comparison to hosted pricing, and (B) a throughput/reserved-capacity model that maps to expected GPU footprint + license, which is more common for Private deals.

Next steps: Marissa will send a cleaner pricing grid and a draft SOW. Can you confirm if you want isolated staging/dev (separate environments) or if shared staging/dev is acceptable? That materially affects the environment adders.

Thanks —
Ben
Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.inference>
To: Alice Chen <alice.chen@payflow.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.inference>
Date: Fri, 02 Jul 2026 09:20:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Redwood Private / VPC Pricing — follow-up: token volumes & licensing

Hi Alice — jumping in with a clearer breakdown and two presentable pricing models. I kept the tone conservative so your procurement team has something they can review quickly.

Model A — Per-1M token equivalent (simple comparison)
- Note: for Private we translate committed throughput into token-equivalents for benchmarking against hosted prices. This is illustrative only.
  - Tier (12mo commit):
    - 0–1B tokens/month equivalent: $9,500 / 1M tokens
    - 1B–3B tokens/month equivalent: $7,250 / 1M tokens
    - 3B+ tokens/month equivalent: $6,000 / 1M tokens

For your 1.5B/month estimate, the blended effective $/1M would be approx $7,625 (rough calculation across tiers).

Model B — Reserved throughput / capacity + license (recommended for Private)
- Annual platform license: $75,000 (includes control plane + up to 2 environments)
- Environment adders: $10,000/env/year for additional isolated environments (staging/dev)
- DR / warm standby: $15,000/year (if you want a cross-region warm standby)
- Support tiers: Standard = $0 (included, business-hours email + monthly review), Premium = $30,000/year (24x7 on-call, TAM, expedited SLAs)
- Reserved GPU capacity: priced as an annual commitment. For 1.5B tokens/month, approximate reserved footprint = N GPUs (we’ll size in the technical call). Pricing example: equivalent spend on reserved capacity + license in year 1 typically results in an equivalent $/1M tokens in the $6k–$8.5k range depending on model size / batching / quantization gains.

Procurement-friendly example (year 1, 1.5B / month):
- Platform license: $75,000
- Environments (prod + staging+dev isolated): $20,000
- DR warm standby: $15,000 (optional)
- Premium support: $30,000
- Reserved capacity (illustrative): $850,000/year (covers needed GPUs + orchestration for your load)
- -----
- Subtotal (license + env + support + capacity): $990,000/year (illustrative)
- Effective blended $/1M tokens (18B tokens/yr): ~$55 per 1M tokens under this capacity model (note: this metric is not apples-to-apples with hosted per-token charges; reserved models convert to $/1M only for procurement comparisons)

Important: the reserved capacity model above gives you predictable latency and costs and is how most Private customers manage their budgets. The per-1M token model is helpful for benchmarking versus hosted options.

Attachments: Redwood_Private_Pricing_V1.xlsx (finalized grid), SOW_Draft_PayFlowai.pdf (draft SOW)

If the numbers look directionally right, next steps we recommend:
1) Tech-sizing call with our infra team (30–45m) to map your expected concurrency and token shapes to a GPU footprint (we can do this early next week)
2) Procurement call to confirm license term and PO process
3) Provide SOC2 artifacts / timeline and iterate on SOW

If you prefer, Ben and I can join your procurement call to walk this through.

Thanks —
